name: Ferment Underground — Gray-Market Supper Club
creator: Anonymous founding collective (attributed to 'The Brine Council')
description: Operating since 2197 in rotating locations across Tier 1 and Tier 2 — abandoned processing floors, decommissioned water treatment antechambers, once memorably a functional storm drain with seating for thirty — The Ferment Underground hosts monthly supper clubs centered entirely on fermentation: real lacto-fermented vegetables, wild-culture breads, unpasteurized alcohol, and occasionally genuine aged cheese sourced through channels no one discusses. Entry costs Φ45 and is invitation-only, distributed through an encrypted word-of-mouth network. Every meal is cooked and served by volunteers who rotate each session.
cultural_impact: The Ferment Underground became a cultural institution of resistance-through-eating, attracting food scholars, the Gray Zone artists, and increasingly curious Tier 3 regulars who see attending as a statement against corporate food systems — its influence on Meridian's fermentation revival of 2209-2215 was substantial.
controversy: Real fermentation without a HelixCorp Food Safety License carries a Φ8,000 fine and potential facility seizure; the Underground has been raided four times, each time successfully vacated before authorities arrived, leading to widespread suspicion that someone inside Meridian's compliance enforcement is a member.
story_hooks: The Brine Council has announced a special session using ingredients that can only have come from a sealed Tier 5 vertical farm — and no one knows how they got them.
A Tier 5 food investor has been attending the Underground in disguise for six months and is now planning to legitimize and commercialize the concept, with or without the Council's consent.
Someone at the last session was poisoned — not fatally, but deliberately — and the encrypted invitation network has been compromised.
